A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniRestorer work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support comparison, including matching analyses across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments, component ablations, generalization evaluations, and computational measurements in Tables 1–8 and Appendix Table A, alongside qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds routing diagnostics, model-capacity comparisons, lightweight-expert experiments, and unseen-degradation evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed degradation extractor, hierarchical clustering, expert training, dual-router procedure, losses, and instruction mode remain unchanged. The lightweight backbones and additional granularity configurations are experimental variants within this framework; expanded training explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix Table F adds evaluation without task-specific training on RainDrop, TOLED, and UIEB, extending coverage to raindrop removal, under-display-camera restoration, and underwater restoration. Existing single- and mixed-degradation coverage remains. Table 3 also relabels denoising from Urban100 to BSD68 while retaining its scores, leaving that particular dataset identity ambiguous.

E2.justification: The existing main benchmark tables retain their comparator sets. New Appendix Table C evaluates enlarged Restormer-L and PromptIR-L comparators, while Table 7 introduces clustering-only and degradation-router-only comparisons. These are limited additions to the comparison methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces lightweight-expert and enlarged-baseline evaluation configurations, including FP16 training for PromptIR-L, and compares routing against PSNR-maximizing expert choices. Metric reporting also changes: Table 3 becomes PSNR-only, and Section 4.1 reserves Y-channel evaluation for single-task deraining, whereas v1 Table 1 explicitly specifies YCbCr for Rain100L. These are reported protocol differences, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: V2 extends sensitivity tests to 16 degradation groups and four granularity levels, adds router-component ablations, and examines practical versus optimal expert loads. Appendix Tables B–C test efficiency and model-capacity explanations, and Table F tests unseen degradations. The original loss ablation is retained as Appendix Table E, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained uncertainty-learning loss and new routing-accuracy diagnostics concern model behavior, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds capacity, efficiency, routing, and unseen-degradation results; Table F reports 24.91, 29.64, and 18.07 dB for UniRestorer. Existing values also change: Rain100L PSNR/SSIM goes from 43.03/0.991 to 41.68/0.996, and LHP from 31.60/0.879 to 30.04/0.886. These revisions do not establish same-setting performance losses. Table 3 removes SSIM results and aggregate averages.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematics in Equations (1)–(9) and degradation formulas (A)–(F) is retained. Generic hierarchy indexing and expanded explanations do not introduce new theoretical reasoning, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: multi-granularity restoration experts, routing that accounts for degradation-estimation error, and closing the performance gap with single-task models. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for diminishing benefits from finer clustering, sequential expert/router training, and choosing full-network experts. It interprets the scaling comparisons as evidence that parameter count alone does not explain performance. New Appendix I identifies limited training-data scale and incomplete alignment with real-world degradations; the existing discussion of cropping artifacts is retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly details per-task training datasets, Urban100 use for ablations, and retraining/replacement of deraining experts for single-task comparisons. It adds training/inference parameter counts, memory consumption, training hours, and PromptIR-L precision information. Existing optimizer, hardware, and router-architecture details remain. The explicit repository address is removed, leaving only a future-release promise.

R1.justification: Section 2 refines the implicit/explicit MoE comparison and expands discussion of task-specific filters, adapters, LoRA, and full-network experts while shortening other descriptions. Waterloo and FoundIR references are added. LoRA-IR was already referenced in v1; its additional bibliography entry is not a newly introduced work. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites portions of the motivation and related work, distinguishes degradation fineness from the number of granularities, and organizes supplementary material into more specific sections. The main section sequence and most method and conclusion prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 is transposed and substantially condensed. V2 adds several appendix displays combining restoration accuracy, computational costs, routing loads, and unseen-task results, while moving the former Table 7 to Appendix Table E. Figure 3 gains explicit component/expert labels and revised placement. The extensive qualitative comparisons in Appendix Figures B–P remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new capacity and efficiency comparisons, routing diagnostics, and unseen-degradation tests address evidential gaps in v1 and improve transparency. The gains are tempered by removed SSIM and repository-address information, and by Appendix A describing deraining-expert retraining while Table 3 and Section 4.2 retain the claim of no additional training. The unexplained denoising-dataset relabeling also limits clarity. Overall, the empirical case improves, but reporting inconsistencies limit the net gain.
